content.content:
# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never

  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and

  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.

  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.

  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.

  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.

  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,

  revision, spec §11 G-34).

  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one

  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not

  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of

  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and

`rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.
- `edit_graphic.rs` — `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`: every argument
  checked through `model_graphic.rs` BEFORE `edit_clip.rs`'s
  `add_described_clip` (`pub(crate)`, with `Described`) places the clip, so
  the op table's bound probe reaches the side check on any project;
  `set_graphic`'s patch reader takes `name`, `width`, `height`, `length`,
  `props` and refuses `in` by name. With a `schema`, a `null` for a prop
  an action on the clip names stores the schema's default (G-34 (d)).
- `edit_clip.rs` — clip construction and placement callers: `add_clip`, move,
  duplicate, delete, join; move, split, delete and duplicate take a linked
  partner through `edit_link.rs`'s closures. `whole_media_length`,
  `edit_clip_timing.rs`'s `trim_end` and `set_speed` hold a media clip's window INSIDE its file, each
  through `source_window.rs`'s one bound, so
  `in + duration × speed ≤ media.duration` and the plan's segment rate is
  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,
  `edit_nest.rs`'s `unnest` and `edit_background.rs`'s timed plate. Over
  the cap, known debt (below).
- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,
  their speed bounds and clip-relative action rescaling; `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`
  (×12, spec §11 #190) and `speed_limits`, which `rc_speed_limits` publishes;
  `set_speed` takes a `rate` or a `duration` (Fit to duration), exactly one.
  On a ramped clip (SR-19 (a), (b)) both rate edits scale the WHOLE profile
  by one factor (`profile_factors`, None on every constant clip):
  `scaled_profile` scales the base, every end rate and every speed span
  (`scaled_span`, snapped, never clamped, which `rescale_actions` also uses),
  writes an unclamped rate as asked, holds the window, then re-clamps the
  other actions into the held duration through `resnap_actions`.
  `trim_start` advances a graphic's `in` through `graphic_advanced` (no speed,
  no head bound, saturating at 0); `trim_end` leaves `length` alone.
- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and
  audio halves; a pure move out of `edit_clip.rs` (grading L3).
- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized
  footage and honours `canvas.fit_new_clips`; Fill is a REQUIREMENT, ignores
  it, scales up as readily as down and clamps to `SCALE_MAX`); a pure move
  out of `edit_clip.rs` (road map "audio" AP9's toll).
- `edit_link.rs` — linked pairs (format 28, spec §11 AU-90…AU-96): Detach
  Audio's picture and sound name each other in `Clip.linked`. `partner`
  (mutual, one container); `with_links` (the named clips, then each one's
  partner on an UNLOCKED track — `move_clips`, `split_clips`,
  `duplicate_clips`, `nest_clips`, `ripple_delete`) and `delete_closure` (a
  linked sound half named alone goes alone); `settle_links`, which `finish`
  runs BEFORE its identity comparison so no op stores a one-sided link and
  none clears the half it orphaned, and `check_links`, `validate`'s refusal
  of one; `pair_split_halves` and `relink_copies` (`duplicate`, `paste` top
  level and nests, `unnest`); `carried_edge` (`trim_start`, `trim_end`,
  `roll`: the partner whose same edge coincided follows unless `alone`);
  `linked_rate_refusal` (speed, direction and speed-naming actions refused);
  and the one op, `attach_audio`. The shift's half is `edit_time.rs`'s
  `shifted`.
- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve
  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions
  check caller-allocated candidates against the input project; both write
  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on
  exactly the chosen tracks before `finish`. `finish` remains equality first,
  validation second, and does not itself refuse. `Clip::placed` is the one
----
- `edit_canvas.rs` — the document's own shape: `set_canvas` and the three
  things it does to the rest of the document — `check_dimension` (a
  dimension is even, because H.264 encodes in macroblocks), `rescale` (a
  size change moves every clip's `x`, `y` and `scale`, each axis by its own
  ratio and `scale` by the smaller of the two) and `resnap` (a rate change
  normalizes top-level and each stored nest's clip times through `frame_grid.rs`
  and drops the second of two top-level markers a coarser grid lands on one tick).
- `edit_time.rs` — ripple, insert time, `ripple_delete_ranges` (the pairs are
  ordered, MERGED — touching as well as overlapping — then cut and closed
  right to left as ONE edit; the singular delegates to it), `lift_range`
  (the hole left open), `close_gap` (refuses rather than closing part way, and
  refuses naming what is there when `at` is on a clip or nothing follows it,

  freeze frame, `shift_clips`, `shifted` (what a shift moves: every unlocked
  clip at or after the boundary and each one's linked partner;
  `shift_clips` moves exactly that set and answers a refusal, nothing moved,
  when a partner would start before 0), and `locked_track` — THE locked-track
  refusal's sentence, written once here for its three callers
  (`close_gap`, `edit_insert.rs`'s `insert_clip`, `edit_transition.rs`'s
  rippled form), each passing the clause after the comma.
- `edit_edge.rs` · `edit_insert.rs` — the cutting moves that keep something
  fixed on purpose: `slip` and `roll` (a `still` slips the frame it holds;
  any other non-media source is an `Err`; roll's predecessor must end
  EXACTLY at the clip's start); `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip`,
  compositions of split + insert time + add made ONE op so a drop is one
  undo step and carries the rule neither half states — an insert cuts only
  the destination track (and a cut clip's linked partner, AU-92) and then
  shifts every unlocked one.
  `roll` is a front trim on its clip, so it advances `graphic.in` as
  `trim_start` does; the predecessor's end is an end trim and keeps `length`.
- `edit_transition.rs` — the WRITE half of a transition: `set_transition`,
  `set_transition_duration`, `set_gained_transitions` (a clip that gains an
  overlap gains a transition) and `add_transition` (an overlap built from
  the two clips' handles at a hard cut). `transition.rs` is the READ half and

  `edit_transition.rs` under the size rule (road map "audio" AP11's toll, a
  pure move).
- `edit_action.rs` · `edit_nest.rs` · `edit_paste.rs` — the action ops and
  their no-overlap rule, plus `check_end_patch`, the END patch's door: the
  three groups §5.4 allows (a `shape` is an unknown key), a `null` that
  REMOVES at every depth rather than clearing, and `patch.rs`'s walk and
  read per group. The door is composed here because which groups an end
  patch names, and what a `null` in one means, are facts about an ACTION;
  values are deliberately not range-checked, except a graphic prop's end

  `parse_payload` are `pub(crate)`, because `edit_paste_attributes.rs` reads

  `graphic` in a `patch` is `edit_action_graphic.rs`'s arm, read against

1://! Ripple, insert time, range delete, lift, close gap and freeze frame —
2://! spec §6 rows `ripple_delete`, `ripple_delete_range`,
3://! `ripple_delete_ranges`, `lift_range`, `close_gap`, `insert_time` and
4://! `freeze_frame`, and the §11 decisions they implement.
5://!
6://! What separates these from `edit_clip.rs`'s ops is that they move
7://! material they were never given: closing or opening a hole in the cut
8://! shifts clips the caller did not name, on tracks the caller did not name.
9://! Three rules run through all of it (spec §11):
10://!
11://! 1. **Ripple is timeline-wide.** A ripple shifts every UNLOCKED track,
12://!    not only the tracks the removed clips were on — that is the one
13://!    behaviour that keeps a music bed in sync with the
14://!    picture it was cut to.
15://! 2. **Locked tracks never move.** Locking a track is how the user says
16://!    "this stays where it is", and it is the only protection from a
17://!    timeline-wide shift.
18://! 3. **Straddling clips stay put.** A clip that covers a boundary is not
19://!    cut by a shift; only clips that begin at or after the boundary move.
20://!    Clips never push each other, and a shift never splits anything the
21://!    user did not ask to split.
22://!
23://! Everything here is composed from the primitives in `edit_clip.rs` —
24://! `split_clips`, `split_under_playhead`, `snapped`, `finish` — rather than
25://! restating them, so a split made by a range delete is the same split ⌘T
26://! makes.
34:/// Default freeze length (spec §6). Two seconds is long enough for a hold
35:/// to read as deliberate and short enough that the user trims it rather
36:/// than deletes it.
39:/// A half-open span of project time a ripple removes.
46:/// The spans merged into disjoint ones, ascending.
47:///
48:/// Adjacent spans merge as well as overlapping ones: two clips that meet at
49:/// a cut leave ONE hole, and shifting twice by two lengths is the same as
50:/// shifting once by their sum only when the boundaries are handled in one
51:/// piece. Empty spans are dropped — a zero-length hole moves nothing.

///
/// Laid out by hand — rustfmt's sixty-character budget for a call's
/// arguments would break all but the shortest row into four lines and cost
/// this file the 400-line cap the deepening gave it. Every line here is
/// inside the same 100 columns rustfmt keeps.
#[rustfmt::skip]
pub const OP_TABLE: [OpRow; OP_COUNT] = [
    // ---- clips ----------------------------------------------------------
    op("add_clip", &[req("track", Id), req("media", Id), req("at", Ticks)]),
    op("add_text_clip",
       &[req("track", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks), opt("text", Object)]),
    op("add_shape_clip",
       &[req("track", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks), opt("shape", Object)]),
    op("add_graphic_clip",
       &[req("track", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks), req("name", Text),
         within(opt("width", Id), GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE, GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE),
         within(opt("height", Id), GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE, GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE),
         opt("props", Object), opt("schema", Object)]),
    op("add_adjustment_clip", &[req("track", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks)]),
    op("add_background", &[opt("media", Id), opt("color", Color), opt("duration", Ticks)]),
    op("add_blurred_background", &[req("clip", Id)]),
    op("insert_clip", &[req("track", Id), req("media", Id), req("at", Ticks)]),
    op("overwrite_clip", &[req("track", Id), req("media", Id), req("at", Ticks)]),
    op("move_clip", &[req("clips", Ids), req("delta", Ticks), opt("track", Id)]),
    op("trim_start", &[req("clip", Id), req("to", Ticks), opt("alone", Boolean)]),
    op("trim_end", &[req("clip", Id), req("to", Ticks), opt("alone", Boolean)]),
    op("rate_stretch", &[req("clip", Id), req("to_end", Ticks)]),
    op("slip", &[req("clip", Id), req("delta", Ticks)]),
    op("roll", &[req("clip", Id), req("to", Ticks), opt("alone", Boolean)]),
    op("split", &[opt("clips", Ids), req("at", Ticks)]),
    op("delete", &[req("clips", Ids)]),
    op("ripple_delete", &[req("clips", Ids)]),
    op("ripple_delete_range", &[req("from", Ticks), req("to", Ticks)]),
    op("ripple_delete_ranges", &[req("ranges", Ranges)]),
    op("lift_range", &[req("from", Ticks), req("to", Ticks)]),
    op("insert_time", &[req("at", Ticks), req("length", Ticks)]),
    op("close_gap", &[req("track", Id), req("at", Ticks)]),
    op("set_speed",
       &[req("clip", Id), opt("rate", Number), opt("duration", Ticks), opt("keep_pitch", Boolean)]),
    op("set_reversed", &[req("clip", Id), req("reversed", Boolean)]),
    op("freeze_frame", &[req("clip", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks)]),
    op("detach_audio", &[req("clip", Id)]),
    op("attach_audio", &[req("clip", Id)]),
    op("duplicate", &[req("clips", Ids)]),
    op("paste", &[req("at", Ticks), opt("track", Id), req("payload", Object)]),
    op("paste_attributes",
       &[req("clips", Ids), req("payload", Object), opt("groups", Groups),
         opt("skip_missing", Boolean)]),
    op("nest", &[req("clips", Ids), opt("name", Text)]),
    op("unnest", &[req("clip", Id)]),
    op("set_video", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object)]),
    op("set_audio", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object)]),
    op("set_text", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object)]),
    op("set_shape", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object)]),
    op("set_graphic", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object), opt("schema", Object)]),
    op("set_clip", &[req("clips", Ids), req("patch", Object)]),
    op("set_enabled", &[req("clip", Id), opt("video", Boolean), opt("audio", Boolean)]),
    op("set_transition", &[req("clip", Id), opt("kind", Transition)]),
    op("set_transition_duration", &[req("clip", Id), req("duration", Ticks)]),
    op("add_transition",
       &[req("clip", Id), opt("kind", Transition), req("duration", Ticks),
         opt("align", Alignment), opt("ripple", Boolean)]),
    op("set_transition_style",
       &[req("clip", Id), opt("curve", Curve), opt("audio", Boolean),
         opt("audio_shape", FadeShape)]),

    // ---- actions --------------------------------------------------------
    op("add_action", &[req("clip", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks)]),
    op("add_zoom_action",
       &[req("clip", Id), req("at", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks), opt("region", Region),
         opt("fit", Fit), opt("curve", Curve)]),
    op("add_speed_ramp",
       &[req("clip", Id), req("shape", RampShape), req("rate", Number), opt("from", Ticks),
         opt("to", Ticks), opt("curve", Curve), opt("hold", Number)]),
    op("set_action",
       &[req("clip", Id), req("action", Id), opt("start", Ticks), opt("duration", Ticks),
         opt("curve", Curve)]),
    op("set_action_end",
       &[req("clip", Id), req("action", Id), req("patch", Object), opt("off", Texts),
         opt("schema", Object)]),
    op("remove_action", &[req("clip", Id), req("action", Id)]),

    // ---- tracks, markers, canvas, media ---------------------------------
    op("add_track", &[opt("index", Index), opt("name", Text)]),
    op("remove_track", &[req("track", Id), opt("with_clips", Boolean)]),
    op("move_track", &[req("track", Id), req("index", Index)]),
    op("set_track",
       &[req("track", Id), opt("name", Text), opt("hidden", Boolean), opt("muted", Boolean),
         opt("locked", Boolean), opt("solo", Boolean), opt("matte", Matte),
         opt("volume", Number), opt("pan", Number), opt("compressor", Object),
         opt("limiter", Object)]),
    op("remove_empty_tracks", &[]),
    op("add_marker",
       &[req("at", Ticks), opt("name", Text), opt("chapter", Boolean), opt("color", Text)]),
    op("set_marker",
       &[req("marker", Id), opt("time", Ticks), opt("name", Text), opt("chapter", Boolean),
         opt("color", Text)]),
    op("remove_marker", &[req("marker", Id)]),
    op("set_canvas",
       &[within(opt("width", Id), CANVAS_MIN, CANVAS_MAX),
         within(opt("height", Id), CANVAS_MIN, CANVAS_MAX),
         opt("fps", FrameRate), opt("background", Color),
         opt("rescale_clips", Boolean), opt("fit_new_clips", Boolean),
         opt("timecode_frames", Boolean), opt("output", Output),
         opt("blending", Blending)]),
    op("add_media", &[req("descriptor", Object)]),
    op("relink_media",
       &[req("media", Id), req("path", Text), opt("bookmark", Text), opt("probe", Object)]),
    op("remove_media", &[req("media", Id), opt("with_clips", Boolean)]),
    op("set_media_color", &[req("media", Id), req("color", Object)]),
    op("set_media_speech", &[req("media", Id), req("spans", Ranges)]),
];

/// Every op name, in table order — a projection of [`OP_TABLE`], not a
/// second list beside it.
///
/// Re-exported by `edit.rs` under the name and path it has always had, so
/// the FFI, the tests and the app all read it exactly where they did. It is
/// kept next to [`Op`] so a mistyped op can be answered with the list
/// instead of a bare parse error — models and users both mistype op names,
/// and the alternative is a serde message written in variant-speak.
///
/// [`Op`]: crate::edit::Op
pub const OP_NAMES: [&str; OP_COUNT] = names();

/// [`OP_TABLE`]'s names, read out at compile time.
const fn names() -> [&'static str; OP_COUNT] {
    let mut names = [""; OP_COUNT];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < OP_COUNT {
        names[i] = OP_TABLE[i].name;
        i += 1;
    }
    names
}

content.content:
swaps the asset.
- `SourceMap.swift` — a media clip's source map (speed ramps SR-20): the
  core's `[clip tick, source tick]` pairs, and the ONE place Swift reads
  between them (linearly, as the ramp renderer plays them; no rate computed
  here, D2-1). Checked ONCE on decode, read by BINARY SEARCH both ways
  (`source(atClip:)`, `clip(atSource:)`), because a ramp holds a point every
  600 ticks and the waveform and the silence walk read per column and per
  bucket; `SourceMaps` is how a reader is handed the maps of its snapshot's
  handle. A reader takes the map only when it is `ramped`, so a constant
  clip keeps today's arithmetic exactly. `rate` is the core's rate profile
  (`RatePoint`s, SR-26), checked on decode; a list that fails the check is
  [] and the map is kept. `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` is
  the filmstrip's and the waveform's map-aware `sourceTime`
  (`TimelineView.swift` is frozen; it holds only `sourceMaps`, set in
  `refreshTimeline` from the same handle as the snapshot).
- `DuckSpeech.swift` — Duck by Speech's Swift half (spec §11 AU-110, AU-111,
  AU-113): `spans` (VAD probabilities → source-tick spans: p ≥
  `defaultVoiceConfidence`, gaps under 0.2 s bridged, ends clamped to the
  media's duration), `ops` (the `set_media_speech` each media without spans
  needs, or a `Refusal` naming the clip or the file), `problem` (the same
  answer without reading a cache, for the popup), and `DuckCurves` (one
  handle's plan `ducks`, decoded lazily once, for the timeline). Every duck
  edit of a Speech duck, in the Ducking section and over `set_audio`, puts
  `ops` before the `set_audio`. No span→time or gain arithmetic: that is
  the core's.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**The editor.**
- `EditorViewController+Graphics` refreshes the paused frame on
  `.projectGraphicsDidChange` for its own document.
- `EditorViewController+Panes.swift` — `PaneSplitView`, whose
  `isDraggingDivider` is true only inside `mouseDown(with:)` (AppKit's divider
  drag), and `savePaneSize`: the timeline height and inspector width are saved
  only from a person's drag of their divider, never a window resize, a
  restore or Hide Inspector (#327; since macOS 12 every resize notification
  carries `NSSplitViewDividerIndex`, so that key cannot tell them apart).
- `EditorViewController+Timeline` / `+Canvas` / `+Inspector` / `+Toolbar` —
  installing the three panes and the toolbar (transport · timecode — view ·
  Export, nothing else). `+Timeline` holds the delete family, including ⌫
  with a range and nothing selected, which LIFTS, and ⌫ with an action
  selected, which removes the action. `+Actions` selects an action (the
  playhead to its end FIRST, then `document.selectAction`), leaves the mode
  (esc, `case 27` in `handleEditorKey`, false when nothing was selected),
  removes the selected one, and selects what ⌥⌘K, Zoom to Region and Zoom
  Back just added.
- `InspectorLabels.swift` — a pure move out of `InspectorPane.swift` (speed
  ramps SR5-0): the small labels and fields every section uses,
  `InspectorRowLabel`, `InspectorMixedBadge`, `InspectorTimecodeField`,
  `InspectorNoteLabel` and `InspectorTextArea` (whose text view routes K-2's
  Return, applying by handing first responder to the content view, K-4).
  `InspectorNoteLabel(wraps:)`
  with `wraps: true` is the one wrapping note: Motion's zero-duration note,
  Speed's silent-audio note and the Clip tab's matte note (#358).
- `InspectorViewController.swift` (frozen: the tab strip, and the PINNED
  container between it and the scroll view that hosts a pane's
  `pinnedBlock`, one generation retired like the strip; the FOOT container
  under the scroll view, collapsed at priority 1 like the pinned one, which
  hosts `refusalStrip`, and the first line of `refresh(isLive:)` that
  clears a stale refusal; `selectClipSubTab`
  is a sub-tab pick's one refresh, and `refresh(isLive:)` calls
  `ClipPane.forgetSubTab()` whenever the selection's ids change, spec §11
  CI-5; a changed selection switches to Clip only from the Media and
  Document tabs, never from the Assistant tab, and `clipPicked()` from any,
  spec §11 AI-14; `onAssistantView` hands the editor the Assistant tab's view;
  `assistantBadge`, the Assistant tab's question dot, installed over the strip
  as the root's last subview, spec §11 AI-19)
  · `InspectorClipView.swift` (the inspector scroll view's clip view,
  installed first: a width change re-lays its document view, so a pane follows
  an autohiding legacy scroller, #142) · `InspectorRefusalStrip.swift` (spec
  §11 CI-10: "Refused: " and the
  core's sentence verbatim, remembered with the `editedProject` handle it
  was shown under and cleared on the first refresh under another handle or
  a click; `showRefusal` is the editor's forward of
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse`) · `InspectorTabBadge.swift` (spec §11 AI-19: the
  Assistant tab's question dot, a passive view over the tab strip — `hitTest`
  nil — mirroring `PanelTabsView.tabRect`'s arithmetic, since `Controls.swift`
  is not forked; `showAssistantBadge(_:)` is its inspector-side setter) ·
  `InspectorPane.swift`
  (the pane base — `pinnedBlock` is the header `makeHeader()` built, never
  stacked; `commandButton(_:_:toolTip:enabled:)`, every section's one-click
  command button such as Crop on Canvas or Detach Audio, #358 — and
  `InspectorBinding` — the one place that knows the fields read the
  SELECTED action's END state
  (`action(_:)` answers the selected action and never consults the playhead;
  `evaluated(_:)` asks `clip_state` at `clip.start + action.endTime`, spec
  §11 CI-2, or in `at(.start)` / `at(.playhead)` at the action's start or
  the playhead, over a cache keyed by clip and `ReadMode`; `.defaults` is
  what a row resets to — `VideoProps.identity`, `AudioProps()`,
  `TextProps()`, `ShapeProps()` — with no FFI and no cache entry, CI-9;
  `graphicProps(_:)` — a graphic clip's props in the binding's mode (the END with an action
  selected, the stored props with none), `[:]` in `.defaults`)) ·
  `InspectorRows.swift` (a pure move out of `InspectorPane.swift`, B87: the row builders, whose
  four typed ones derive a row's DEFAULT from its own `read` and `ops` unless `resets: false`;
  `inspectorRow(discrete:)` makes a row discrete — "at end" — when its control is none of the
  popup, checkbox or segmented control: the graphic string row and the Text tab's Content area;
  a row's widest `OptionPopupControl` — or, in a row with none, its widest
  `OptionCheckboxControl`, clipped to its bounds so its title stops at its edge — holds its
  intrinsic width only at compression resistance 749, below the one-line tag's 750, so a keyed
  row short of room narrows that control and never the tag (O8, G-34 (l): Font ▸ Family, a
  filter's and an obscure region's kind, a module's boolean with a long label); and an
  `InspectorNameField` — a graphic's one-line string, a marker's name — takes the row's width,
  hugging at 1 with no trailing spacer and resisting compression at 248, below the tag (G-48)) ·
  `InspectorSlider.swift` (`InspectorSliderControl`, a pure move: the 7 × 11
  block knob snapped to device pixels (CI-6) and, keyed, the mint segment
  from the action's start value and the coral playhead tick; it maps and
  draws through `InspectorRail.swift`, which `WheelStripControl` shares, the
  keyed knob's ink passed in: textStrong here, CI-6, the action ink there,
  §4.3b, #358) ·
  `ColorWheelControl.swift` (`ColorWheelControl`: a hue disc drawn at
  `hueRotation` 103° so each hue sits near its vectorscope target, its 7 × 7
  square puck dragged as a live edit by the pointer's delta, ⌥ a tenth, clamped
  to the rim, double-click resets the push; spec §11 GR-11) ·
  `WheelStripControl.swift` (`WheelStripControl`: the master strip with the
  slider's knob, a press on the knob grabs it, elsewhere jumps, ⌥ drags relative
  at a tenth, double-click resets, one undo step on or off the knob, #272;
  its rail is `InspectorRail.swift`'s) ·

two widths closer.
  - A preference for breaking at a clause mark.
  - A lone over-wide word shrinks in 5 % steps down to 80 %, then wraps at
    the budget width.
  - A page ends at `min(next.start, last.end + hold)`, extended to the next
    page when the gap is under `breakGap`: no blink.

**Pauses come from word gaps of 0.25 s plus sentence punctuation. The
silence detector is not consulted (W-7; orig §5c, §10.9).**
`SpeechTranscriber`'s word ranges TILE the audio: a 1.57 s real silence
showed as a 0.30 s gap, and a 1.13 s one as 0.06 s. So the literature's
0.4 s `breakGap` found nothing, and 0.25 s was chosen. W4a injected road map
4's detector pauses as forced breaks and got the same ten pages, because the
punctuation already broke there.

**Each engine has its own `lead`, applied once in `normalize` and never to
Subtitles (W-7).** On-device is +270 ms: the engine starts words early.
AssemblyAI is −60 ms. Both are W0 q2's signed medians against known onsets.
They are starting points for a person to adjust by eye, not a calibration.

**A page is confined to its job's clip span (W-7; orig §10.9).** Neither
`lead` nor `hold` carries a page past its clip. A word pushed off the end
sits on the clip's last frame. `Transcriber.Job.span` is the one place that
span is spelled.

**A shrunk page is one construction in three places (W-7; orig §10.10
residue).** `CaptionStyle.textProps` is what the pager measures and the
preview draws. `pagePatch`, built from it, is what `place` writes. So the
outline is em × the SHRUNK size everywhere.

**macOS 26 minimum, with `SpeechAnalyzer`/`SpeechTranscriber` replacing
`SFSpeechRecognizer` (W-8; orig §5f, §5g, §10.4, §10.6).**
- `SpeechEngine.swift` is the one new `async` file. Callers use synchronous
  wrappers.
- Deleted: the one-minute ceiling (W0 found none: 99.81 % of a 613 s file
  came back); the TCC grant (none needed, even in a hardened-runtime bundle
  without the usage key); `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`; and
  `transcribe`'s `truncated` and `note` keys.
- The bump cost three new `AVMutableVideoComposition` deprecation warnings,
  so the typecheck baseline is now 7. `AVVideoComposition.Configuration` was
  not adopted.

content.content:
# Settings

Frame Job keeps the things that belong to you, not to a project, in one
window: how an MCP client reaches the app, your Anthropic key and the
assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region for cloud transcription,
and whether graphics render in the background while you are idle. This page
covers every control in that window, the View-menu choices Frame Job
remembers between launches, and where the app keeps its files on disk.

## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,). It works with or without a project
open, so you can set keys from the Welcome window before you make anything.
The Assistant tab also opens it for you: when no Anthropic key is set, it
shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an
**Open Settings…** button. The Generate Captions sheet only tells you where
to go: with AssemblyAI chosen and no key set, the note under its button reads
"No AssemblyAI API key is set — Frame Job ▸ Settings…".

Settings is one window, not a set of tabs. It holds four sections, top to
bottom: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. On a
short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls. Closing it
loses nothing: every control saves as you use it, or when you press its
**Save** button, as described below. While it is open it is listed in the
**Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ button.
Rest the pointer on it for a moment to see that section's explanation; click
it to keep the explanation open, and click it again (or anywhere else, or
press Escape) to close it.

*Agents:* no MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Keys, the model,
the region and Background render are set only by a person in this window.
An agent's cloud tools (`transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine,
`transcribe_for_fillers`) do use the key and region saved here, so a person
must set the key first; without one they refuse with "No AssemblyAI API key
is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings ▸ Transcription…".

## MCP


There is nothing to tune. Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut:

- The cut widens outward to a 32 ms speech grid so the whole filler goes, but it never reaches into the words on either side.
- Its edges then snap inward to the frame grid, as Remove Silences does. A tiny filler can end up too short to cut.
- A filler is **left in whole**, never trimmed, when cutting it would reach into a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, into a nest clip, or into a transition. The sheet counts these: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."
- A clip on a locked track isn't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet says how many such clips there are.
- A clip that plays in reverse, whose sound is switched off, whose media file is missing, or whose media has no audio track has no words to read. When nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."

**Which clips:** the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file (the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read."), otherwise every clip. There is no scope menu.

### Filler words need a cloud transcript

Filler words come only from an **AssemblyAI** transcript made with filler words. Transcription on your Mac doesn't report them reliably. This makes filler removal a cloud feature: you need an AssemblyAI API key, set in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,) under **Transcription**.

Every AssemblyAI transcription Frame Job makes asks for filler words. Any file you caption with AssemblyAI (**File ▸ Generate Captions…**, AssemblyAI engine) is therefore already ready for Remove Filler Words, with no second upload. Only files never transcribed in the cloud, or transcribed before filler words were requested, are listed in the sheet.

When a file in scope has no such transcript, the sheet lists it under "Filler words are found only in an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words — transcription on this Mac does not report them. These files have none yet:". Each listed file gets a row with:

- its name;
- the estimate: what would be uploaded and what it would cost, at the rate shown in the tooltip;
- a **Transcribe** button.

Above the rows, the sheet says where the audio goes: "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Transcribe is pressed." It names European Union instead when that region is set in Settings.

Pressing **Transcribe** sends one file:

- It reuses that file's earlier transcription choices (language, speaker labels and vocabulary) and adds filler words. A file never transcribed before uses language detection, no speakers and no vocabulary.
- A file listed here that already has a caption transcript is uploaded again: that older transcript was made without filler words, so this is a second paid transcription.
- It only updates the project's saved transcript for that file. It places no captions and adds no undo step.
- The new transcript also serves captions: a later **File ▸ Generate Captions…** with AssemblyAI reuses it for that file instead of uploading again.
- While it runs, the row shows its progress, its button reads **Stop**, the other rows' buttons are disabled, and **Remove** is disabled. Return can't make a cut in the middle of a paid upload.
- When it finishes, the file drops off the list and its fillers join the count. If the run failed, the reason appears in the note.

**Transcribe** is disabled with no API key (the note points to **Frame Job ▸ Settings…**), for a file no clip plays, and while another file's run is going. A project you haven't saved yet can be transcribed; its transcript is kept with the project when you save. Closing the sheet stops a run in progress.

### Captions stay clean

Filler words never reach your captions. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** removes them from every transcript before making captions, so a transcript made with filler words produces the same captions as one made without them. See [Captions](captions.md).

*Agents:* `detect_fillers` answers the ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. It takes `clips` and lists each kept run under `fillers`, each left-in run under `dropped` with its reason, files with no filler transcript under `needs_transcript`, and locked clips under `locked`. It also answers `count`, `removes`, `scope` and `clips`, plus `skipped` when `clips` is given (each named clip it couldn't read, with the reason). Pass its `ranges` to `ripple_delete_ranges`. `transcribe_for_fillers` (`media`) is the Transcribe button: a paid upload that answers `ready` when `detect_fillers` can read that file. On a media that already has a filler transcript it uploads nothing and answers `ready: true`; otherwise it answers `uploaded`, `cached`, `audio_seconds`, `engine` and `language`. It is refused with no AssemblyAI key and for a media no clip plays. The built-in assistant can't use it.

## Reading a clip's transcript

An agent can read the words of any clip that plays speech from a media file, each with its start and end in timeline time. The times can be passed directly to a cut.

- **Where the words come from.** The file's saved AssemblyAI transcript when it has a current one. Otherwise this Mac's own speech recogniser runs over the clip, which takes a few seconds per minute of speech. Reading a transcript never uses the network and never uploads anything.
- **Fillers are flagged.** Each word says whether it is a filler. The answer also says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all. An on-device transcript never is, so a filler can be in the audio but missing from the words.
- **A part of the clip.** A `from`/`to` window in timeline time returns only the words that overlap it; a word crossing an edge comes back whole. With a window, the on-device recogniser hears only that part plus 2 seconds on each side. It is faster, but with less context a windowed answer can differ slightly from a whole-clip one. Either end may be given alone: a missing `from` is the clip's start and a missing `to` its end. The window is clamped to the clip and echoed back as `from`/`to`. An empty window, or one outside the clip, is refused.
- **Saved for next time.** What the on-device recogniser heard is saved in the project, per media file and language. A later request inside a stretch it has already heard comes back at once, even from another clip of the same file at any speed. A saved on-device transcript is used only while the media file and the macOS version are unchanged (the recogniser ships with macOS).
- **Speed and ramps.** Words are placed through the clip's speed, including a speed ramp, so their times match what plays on the timeline.
- **Stopping a read.** An on-device read can be long. The assistant's **Stop** ends it, and nothing is saved from a stopped read.
- **Language.** On-device recognition uses this Mac's language unless another tag (such as `en-US`) is given. A language whose speech model isn't installed is refused. Agents never download one; you can install it from **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

*Agents:* `get_transcript` (`clip`, optional `language`, `from`, `to`) answers `words` (`text`, `start`, `end`, `filler`, and `speaker` when known), `fillers_reported`, `engine` and, for an on-device answer, `cached`. It edits nothing.

## Cutting false starts with the assistant

A false start is a phrase the speaker abandoned or said again. Deciding what counts is a judgement about meaning, so there is no menu command for it. Ask the assistant in the inspector's Assistant tab instead, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip." The assistant:

1. reads the clip's words and their times;
2. tells you which words it will cut;
3. cuts them in one step, each cut running from the first cut word's start to the last cut word's end.

It cuts false starts only when you ask. It can also remove fillers the same way **Remove Filler Words** does, and take out silences the way **Remove Silences** does (`detect_silence`, then one `ripple_delete_ranges`). Any cut an agent makes this way, whether silences, fillers or false starts, is one undo step labelled **Undo Ripple Delete**, not the sheet's name. The assistant can't start a paid filler transcription: press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself. See [The assistant](assistant.md).

## Limits

- **Filler removal is cloud-only.** Without an AssemblyAI key, filler words can't be found. A project transcribed before filler words were requested is transcribed again, and billed again, before its fillers can be cut.
- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. A filler it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in captions.
- **Protection needs a transcript.** A filler cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a transcript. Speech on another unlocked track with no transcript isn't protected.
- **Up to a frame can remain.** Inward frame snapping can leave a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind.
- **Wait for analysis.** After import, Remove Silences proposes nothing inside a file until its analysis is ready: the waveform in Level mode, the voice analysis in Voice mode (and the waveform too for a clip with no voice), except where the mix already makes it quiet.
- **Voice mode can miss a soft first word** in a quiet recording; raise **Keep at ends:** if a word is clipped.
- **Singing and voice-like instruments** may read as speech.
- **A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length**, so a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level. Limit the scope (**In:** Selected clips) to keep music out.

content.content:
*Agents:* `add_marker {at?, name?, chapter?, color?}` (at the playhead when
`at` is left out), `set_marker {marker, time?, name?, chapter?, color?}`,
`remove_marker {marker}`.

## The in/out range

The in/out range is a span of the timeline shaded across the ruler and the
lanes. It sets what Loop plays, what ⌫ lifts and ⌘⌫ ripple-deletes when no
clip is selected (see [Editing](editing.md)), the span a speed ramp preset
covers when it lies inside the clip (see [Speed](speed.md)), what a new
adjustment clip covers (see [Colour grading](color-grading.md)), and what an
export writes when you choose the range.

| Key | Menu | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| I | **Mark ▸ Set In** | Sets the in point at the playhead. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline. |
| O | **Mark ▸ Set Out** | Sets the out point at the playhead. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start. |
| ⌥X | **Mark ▸ Clear Range** | Clears the range (available only while one is set) |

Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and
the other way round. The range is view state (not an undo step, not saved),
and it's cleared whenever you enter or leave a nest.

*Agents:* `set_range {start?, end?}` (no bounds clears it).

## Clip names and labels
9:Most commands act on the **selection**, the clips outlined in coral on the timeline. Some also use the **playhead**, the **in/out range**, or the **current track**:
13:- **The in/out range.** I sets the in point, O sets the out point and ⌥X clears both (**Mark ▸ Set In / Set Out / Clear Range**). With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range instead.
18:*Agents:* `set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the same view state. They are not edits and make no undo step.
100:The two delete keys pair up. Each acts on the selection, or on the in/out range when nothing is selected. The difference is whether the hole closes.
102:| Command | Selection | In/out range, nothing selected |
104:| **Edit ▸ Delete** (⌫) | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range and removes what lies between. Nothing moves, markers included. |
105:| **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** (⌘⌫, or the timeline bar's button) | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips, then closes each hole they leave. Everything later on every unlocked track moves left by the hole's length. | **Ripple Delete:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range, removes what lies between, and closes the hole. |
109:- Both items are greyed out while you are typing in a text field, so ⌫ and ⌘⌫ still edit text there. They are also greyed out when nothing is selected and no range is set.
112:*Agents:* `delete` and `ripple_delete` take `clips`. `lift_range` and `ripple_delete_range` take `from` and `to`; a reversed pair means the same range. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes a list of `[from, to]` pairs. It merges pairs that touch or overlap, then cuts them all as one edit.
149:**Paste** keeps the copied arrangement. The earliest clip lands at the playhead and the others keep their distance from it. The copied front-most lane goes onto the front track, the lanes behind it onto the tracks behind, and tracks are added at the back if there aren't enough. A pasted clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new track at the front, so a paste is never refused for lack of room. You can paste into another project. Media is matched by file path and added to the project when it isn't there yet. Pasted clips get new identities and are snapped to the project's frame rate.
215:When you go in, the selection is cleared. When you come out, the nest clip is selected again. Going in and coming out aren't edits: there is no undo step, and the project isn't marked as changed. The in/out range is cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline.
253:- **A menu command or key** is one step, even when it changes many clips. Examples: Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection, a Remove Silences pass.
255:- **No step at all** for anything that doesn't change the project: selecting, moving the playhead, setting the in/out range, going into or out of a nest, a refused edit, and an edit that would leave everything as it was.
265:An edit that would change nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage or a paste of a look the clips already have, beeps too, but shows no message: no rule was broken. A request the project can't use at all, such as a pasted value outside its allowed range, shows an error alert instead.
275:- **Locked tracks.** Their clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and a marquee doesn't select them. Split with nothing selected, Lift, and the range form of Ripple Delete leave them uncut. Ripples, gap closes and inserted time don't shift them. Insert onto a locked track and Close Gap on a locked track are refused. A clip on a locked track that you select by clicking is still removed by Delete or Ripple Delete, and Overwrite still clears a locked track.
287:| ⌫ | Delete the selection, or lift the in/out range |
288:| ⌘⌫ | Ripple delete the selection or the in/out range |

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);
a citation of the bare number names them together, and this index gets their rows in the same
change. Until #342 (2026-10-24) §4.3b was the Media, Document and Assistant tabs, now §4.3c; an older citation of §4.3b (in `archive/` or git history) means §4.3c.

The Lines column is `wc -l`; the `11-decisions/` cell is that folder's total, its README
included, and `make test` checks both (`tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`).

## The original preface

**Status: accepted and built** (M1–M3, then road maps 2–12; `designs/adr/` has each one's
record). The preface below is the original handoff's, kept for its reading order.

Sibling of `~/devel/rasterize` — the same shape (Swift/AppKit app over a Rust staticlib core, a
hand-maintained C header as the one contract, xcodegen, an embedded MCP agent), a different domain.
Where this document says "as in Rasterize" it names the file to copy from.

Reading order for an implementer: §1–2 (the product), §5–7 (model, ops,
architecture — the parts with exact schemas), §10 (build order), then §3–4
when building the UI, §8–9 for conventions and keys, §11 for the decisions
already made so they are not re-litigated.

content.content:
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

content.content:
correct by construction because the plan contains exactly the
  structural facts.
- **Overlap rule**: at most one neighbour per side, each overlap ≤ half
  the shorter clip; larger overlaps refuse. Clips never push.
- **Ripple is timeline-wide** across unlocked tracks; straddling clips
  on other tracks stay put.
- **Freeze frame keeps sync** by inserting time across all unlocked
  tracks, and is a one-source-frame segment scaled in the composition —
  no image extraction.
- **Ducking is by clip extent**, not voice activity,
  so no audio analysis is needed for it.
  **Amended by AU-110** (road map "audio" AP11): extent stays the default, and a duck may
  instead follow the ducking clip's speech, from spans saved on its media.
- **Speed and pitch** come from `scaleTimeRange` and the time-pitch
  algorithm. Reverse is not native; M3 pre-renders reversed segments.
- **Text and shapes are described, not rasterized, in the model.** The
  recipe carries the description; the platform renders it (Core Text /
  CG). Measured text sizes live in a Swift cache, never in the model.
- **Time is 600 000 ticks/s.** Mixed source rates resolve at render, never
  in the model.
- **No left panel.** Media is an inspector tab. Revisit if libraries grow

468:- **GR-9 — The branch wrote project format 1015 and refused 15–1014 by name; at the merge 1015
469-  became 15.** The branch's `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` was **1015** (main's 14 plus a thousand), in
470-  `core/src/format.rs` and the header, so every main build refused a branch-made project as "made
471-  by a newer Frame Job" instead of opening it and dropping its grades on the next save.
472-  Its base version was 14: the branch read 1 to 14 and 1015, and refused a file numbered 15 to
473-  1014 in its own sentence (naming the numbers it reads), because a later main file
474-  would otherwise open and lose its new keys on save (owner choice 9). Above 1015 the existing
475-  "newer" sentence answered. The branch had no migrate step: 1015 is 14 plus optional keys (and, since GR-6,
476-  the `adjustment` source kind, which an older build refuses by name). **At the merge** (GR7b,
477-  2026-10-10) 1015 became **15**, main's next version. A file numbered 1015 is read as 15 by one
478-  migration step (`migrate_1015_to_15` in `format.rs`, run before the "newer" gate, mapping to the
479-  literal 15 so a later bump still runs its own steps from 15; `GRADING_BRANCH_VERSION` names
480-  the number), so branch-made projects still open. The base-version constant and the gap refusal
481-  are gone, and 16 and above, 1014 included, are "newer". Risk accepted: a project the owner saved on
482-  the grading branch opened only there until the merge (he kept his trial projects as copies).

content.content:
- Person checks: GRD-1…GRD-10 in `docs/manual-checks.md`.

**Headline numbers** (Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, `powermode 0`, AC power).

GR0, one ungraded full-bleed layer, overhead over the tree (ms, 1080p / 4K): flag (VF-TL) 0.000 / 0.001; function constants (VC-TL) −0.003 / −0.000; always on (VA-TL) 0.022 / 0.083. T2, a graded layer over its own ungraded figure, flag route: tone only 0.049 / 0.197; tone and a 33³ look 0.057 / 0.226; one full-frame adjustment pass 0.045 / 0.174. The spike's comments in `Compositor.metal` cite the

#258's X1 (GR0, four video layers at 4K): G = H16 − B8 = 0.135 ms, W = H16 − min(X420, X422) = 0.131 ms ≥ 0.5·G, so a 10-bit biplanar source wins back nearly all the half-float source's layer-stage cost; #258 stays open for the owner.

GR7a's caps against main at the branch point `5d04e47`:

| Measure | Cap | Measured | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frozen files | wiring only, ~50 lines | `EditorViewController.swift` +3, the other four net 0: held | `grading_verdict.py sizes` L2 |
| Files over the cap | none unpaid | held after L3: `ProjectSnapshot.swift` 1,750 → 1,570, `edit_clip.rs` 755 → 661 | `sizes` L3 (at `df40ac1`) |
| Inspector | one sub-tab, ≤ 4 sections | Color: Light, Color, Adjustment, Look; Picture −Color: held | `sizes` L4 |
| Menus | the four named items | 175 → 187 leaves, those four, none removed: held | `RC_PROOF_APP=release grading_verdict.py measure --only H0,M1,G0,E1,E2,Z1` M1 |
| An ungraded layer | +0.02 ms 1080p, +0.06 ms 4K | +0.009 / +0.002 ms (C0 noise 0.000): held | `grading_spike.py --measure --tree` TC |
| An ungraded export | ≤ 2 % over main | +0.33 % (6.00 s against 5.98 s, 60 s at 1080p): held | `measure` E1 |
| A graded export | ≤ 10 % over ungraded | −0.17 % (5.99 s against 6.00 s): held | `measure` E2 |
| A graded frame | ≤ 8 ms at 1080p | 2.724 ms median compositor average (worst window 7.07–7.70 ms): held | `RC_PROOF_APP=release grading_verdict.py measure --only H0,F4,T4,Z1` F4 |

The exports are encoder-bound at these sizes, so E1 and E2 say the grade costs no export time on that fixture, not that the compositor does no more work; F4 is the frame-time figure. T4's script half: a 33³ LUT through Frame Job against ffmpeg's `lut3d` on the same frame, max |Δ| 2 levels (the control, no LUT, 56).

## The verdict

The owner, 2026-10-10: "I think we can merge this." And: "T1 and T3 look good to me. I'll get feedback later from others and we can adjust."
- T1 (Light on a warm, dark clip) and T3 (a built-in look): run, good.
- T4 (a LUT): run with test LUTs, not one of his own: "LUT worked".
- T2 (one adjustment clip over a whole video), T5 (the Assistant) and T6 (a power window): not run by the owner; now GRD-7, GRD-8 and GRD-9. GRD-10 is the feedback from others.
- GRD-1…GRD-6: not reported; they stay standing rows.
- Every cap in the table above held.

## Known limits

- **Whether AVFoundation converts log footage** (Apple Log, S-Log, V-Log) before the compositor is not established, and so neither is whether a camera log LUT looks right: no log clip was available (#264).
- **Banding on real footage** is a question about the source's own levels, answered by GR2's fixture and the owner's eye (GRD-1), not by a script.
- **Whether 65³ is worth it for built-in looks** is not measured; a built-in look is defined by its 33³ lattice, so that is not a defect. An imported LUT arrives at its own size.
- **The adjustment clip with Preview Quality and the matte pool** is reasoned from the code, not run.
- **Other editors' behaviour** (adjustment layers reaching every track, scopes as a panel) is from general knowledge.
- **The trial is partial**: T2, T5 and T6 and GRD-1…GRD-10 are the owner's standing checks, and other people's feedback is still to come.

## Open items

Filed or touched at the close; the new ones are each `ai-drafted` and `low-priority`:
- #259: flip_x and flip_y, cut from tier 1 (from #118, closed).
